insertTab.title: Insert proteins from UniProt
insertTab.description: Fetches protein sequences from UniProt in FASTA format and saves each one as a Protein row plus a deduplicated Sequence row. This is always the first step: every other pipeline stage (embeddings, annotation, evaluation) requires proteins and their sequences to be loaded here first.
insertTab.searchCriteriaHelper: UniProt query syntax. E.g. "reviewed:true" = Swiss-Prot only (~600k); "reviewed:true AND organism_id:9606" = reviewed human only.

metadataTab.title: Enrich proteins with UniProt
metadataTab.description: After "Insert proteins" (which only loads accession + sequence), this step fetches each protein's functional record from UniProt and stores it as ProteinUniProtMetadata: name, gene, organism, EC, catalytic activity, active and binding sites, cofactor, pathway, kinetics, keywords, and more. It also backfills the core Protein columns (Swiss-Prot/TrEMBL, organism, length, gene) left empty by the insert. Idempotent: re-running only updates what changed upstream.

onboarding.intro: Functional annotation transfers GO terms from proteins of known function to your query sequences. PROTEA encodes each protein into a high-dimensional embedding, runs a KNN search against a reference annotation set, and aggregates the neighbors' GO terms into a ranked prediction per protein. You need three ingredients before launching a job: precomputed embeddings, a reference annotation set, and the query sequences you want to annotate.
onboarding.prereqsHelper: Each step opens its dedicated page so you can build or pick the artefact.

embeddings.title: Embedding model
embeddings.help: A protein language model (PLM) configuration plus its precomputed vectors over your reference proteins. The KNN search runs in this embedding space, so its choice (esm2, prost_t5, ankh, etc.) determines which proteins look similar.
embeddings.emptyLabel: No embedding configuration is registered yet.

annotationSet.title: Reference annotation set
annotationSet.help: The pool of GO annotations you transfer from. Typically a GOA or QuickGO release filtered by evidence code. Neighbors found by KNN must come from this set, so its coverage and freshness directly limit recall.

scoring.title: Scoring Configs
scoring.labBadgeHint: Research / LAB surface: research and reproducibility parameters are intentionally exposed.
scoring.description: A ScoringConfig defines how raw prediction signals are combined into a single [0, 1] confidence score — without re-running the KNN pipeline.
scoring.pageDescription: After KNN annotation produces a ranked list of candidate GO terms, the scoring layer re-weights those candidates using configurable signal combinations: embedding similarity, sequence alignment identity, GO evidence code quality, and taxonomic proximity. Different configs let you compare scoring strategies on the same prediction set without dispatching new annotation jobs.

formulaHints.linear: Weighted average of active signals: score = sum(w_i * s_i) / sum(w_i). Simple and interpretable.
formulaHints.evidenceWeighted: Same weighted average as linear, then multiplied by the resolved evidence quality weight. Predictions backed only by IEA (electronic) are automatically down-ranked even if their embedding similarity is high.

emptyHero.title: No scoring configs yet
emptyHero.body: Load the built-in presets to start — they cover the most common trade-offs between embedding-only scoring, alignment-boosted scoring, and evidence-weighted scoring. You can then clone and tune them.

signals.evidenceWeightHint: Quality of the reference annotation's GO evidence code.

newConfigForm.systemDefaultsNote: Using system defaults — EXP/IDA → 1.0 · ISS/IBA → 0.7 · IEA → 0.3 · ND → 0.1
newConfigForm.experimentalDescription: Annotations backed by direct experimental evidence. Highest confidence tier.
newConfigForm.computationalDescription: Annotations derived from sequence similarity, orthology, or phylogenetic inference.
newConfigForm.electronicDescription: Automated annotations (IEA) or non-traceable author statements (NAS). Lower confidence.
newConfigForm.noDataDescription: Placeholder code indicating no biological data is available.

page.title: Re-ranker Models
page.labBadgeHint: Research surface: reproducibility parameters are intentionally visible.
page.description: LightGBM binary classifiers that re-score GO predictions using alignment, taxonomy, and aggregate features. Training lives in the offline protea-reranker-lab; this page registers the resulting booster so PROTEA can use it during inference.
page.importBtnHint: Upload the three files from a lab run: model.txt (the LightGBM booster), spec.yaml (experiment spec), and run.json (metrics and provenance). PROTEA stores the booster in the artifact store and records a RerankerModel row.
page.registerBtnHint: The booster already lives in MinIO or the local artifact store. Paste the URI and the spec/run metadata so PROTEA records the row without re-uploading the binary.
page.contextBannerTitle: Register a LightGBM booster trained in protea-reranker-lab
page.contextBannerBody: LightGBM training lives in the offline lab; this page registers the resulting booster so PROTEA can score predictions with it. Use Import booster to upload a fresh model.txt + spec.yaml + run.json, or Register by URI when the artefact already lives in MinIO.

categoryHints.nk: No Knowledge: proteins with zero GO annotations at the training cutoff. The hardest evaluation setting; measures pure prediction ability from sequence alone.
categoryHints.lk: Limited Knowledge: proteins annotated in some GO namespaces but not all at the training cutoff. The booster targets new annotations in previously empty namespaces.
categoryHints.pk: Partial Knowledge: proteins that already had annotations in a namespace at the training cutoff and gained further annotations later. The booster predicts extensions to existing functional profiles.

page.schemaShaHint: feature_schema_sha: family-aware fingerprint of the feature set the booster was trained on. PROTEA refuses to use a booster whose schema does not match the live pipeline.
page.manifestShaHint: dataset_manifest_sha: SHA-256 of the training dataset manifest. A drift here means the lab trained on a different dump than the one registered in the Datasets page.
page.datasetHint: Dataset row that was used for training. Click the name to open the full provenance in the Datasets page.
page.externalSourceHint: Free-form provenance tag recording which external tool and version produced the booster (e.g. protea-reranker-lab@<git-sha>).

apiKeys.title: API keys
apiKeys.subtitle: Programmatic access keys for CLI clients, CI pipelines, and the offline reranker lab. Each key is hashed on the server the moment it is created; the raw value is displayed once and cannot be retrieved again. Rotate keys regularly and revoke any that are no longer in use.

roleDescriptions.viewer: Read-only access to all public endpoints. Use for monitoring dashboards or read-only CI checks.
roleDescriptions.operator: Can dispatch jobs (POST /v1/datasets, POST /v1/jobs), run maintenance, and manage query sets. Required by the reranker lab when pulling datasets or registering boosters.
roleDescriptions.admin: Full control including minting and revoking other API keys, admin-only pages, and destructive operations. Restrict to trusted automation only.

apiKeys.rotationAdvice: Rotate keys every 90 days or immediately after any suspected exposure.
apiKeys.storageAdvice: Store the raw key in a secret manager (e.g. GitHub Actions secrets, Vault). Never commit it to source control.

login.subtitle: Use the email and password you registered with.

errors.pendingApproval: Your account is still pending admin approval. You will be able to sign in once it has been activated.
errors.deactivated: This account has been deactivated. Contact an administrator to re-enable it.
errors.serverUnavailable: Sign-in is not available on this server (JWT secret is not configured).

signup.title: Create a PROTEA account
signup.subtitle: Tell us a little about why you need access. An admin reviews every new account before activation.
signup.usernameHint: Shown on shared resources (jobs, audit log). Letters, digits, dashes.
signup.intendedUseHint: What you plan to do with PROTEA. Helps admins approve faster.
signup.intendedUsePlaceholder: e.g. Benchmarking GO-term predictors on CAFA-style splits.

errors.emailTaken: An account with this email already exists. Try signing in instead.
errors.usernameTaken: That username is already taken. Please pick another one.

profile.anonymousTitle: Sign in to view your profile
profile.anonymousBody: Your account details, role and status appear here once you are signed in.
profile.title: Your profile
profile.subtitle: Account details for {name}.
profile.displayNameBody: Shown next to your jobs, audit-log entries and shared resources.
profile.saveDisabledTitle: The PATCH /auth/me endpoint is not yet wired. Display name edits land in a follow-up auth slice.
profile.saveDisabledNote: Editing is disabled in this build (no profile-update endpoint on the current server). It will activate automatically once the backend exposes the corresponding mutation.

pendingApproval.title: Account pending admin approval
pendingApproval.body: Your account request has been recorded. An administrator will review your intended use and activate the account. You will be able to sign in once that happens.
pendingApproval.note: Approvals are usually processed within a working day. If you have not heard back after that, please ping the project maintainer through the documentation contact.

errors.title: This view could not be loaded
errors.body: The interface hit an error while building this page. What the app reported is shown below.
errors.unauthorizedBody: The server withheld this data because the request carried no valid session. Sign in, then retry.
errors.forbiddenTitle: You are not permitted to view this
errors.forbiddenBody: Your account is missing the role this page requires. Ask an administrator to grant it, then retry.
errors.networkTitle: The server could not be reached
errors.networkBody: The request never completed. Check that the backend is running and reachable, then retry.

notFound.title: This page does not exist
notFound.body: The address matched no route. Check the link, or return to the start page.

predictionSetNotFound.title: This prediction set does not exist
predictionSetNotFound.body: No prediction set matches this id. It may have been deleted, or the id is wrong.

featureRegistry.title: Feature registry
featureRegistry.subtitle: Every reranker feature has one canonical description, shared by the documentation, the thesis, and this page. Here you can read what each feature means, who produces it, and whether it carries a real value in the default export.
featureRegistry.provenance: Sourced from protea-contracts {version}. {total} features across {families} families.

PRODUCED.label: produced
PRODUCED.help: Filled with a real value in the default export.

DECLARED_ABSENT.label: declared absent
DECLARED_ABSENT.help: Left unfilled by the default export because its producer is not wired into the export path (ADR-D45). The value you see in a raw dump is not the model's signal.

POOL_INJECTED.label: pool injected
POOL_INJECTED.help: Stamped by the lab's pooled multi-manifest loader at pool stage. It does not appear in a raw parquet dump.

BROKEN.label: broken
BROKEN.help: The producer is wired but its data source is empty or faulty, so the column carries no signal.
